fields.label: Flag state
fields.help: The Norwegian cargo-ship rules specify Norwegian ships. The 12-passenger instrument also covers foreign vessels in the specified waters.

fields.label: Ship type
fields.help: Use the vessel’s statutory class. The Norwegian small cargo-ship regulations name cargo ships.

fields.label: Regulatory length (L)
fields.help: Use the length defined in the Load Lines Convention applicable when the ship was built. Consult the vessel’s statutory particulars.

fields.label: Length overall (største lengde)
fields.help: Enter the overall length recorded for the vessel. Sections 1 and 2 use different length measurements.

fields.label: Gross tonnage
fields.help: Use the gross tonnage figure on the tonnage certificate. Cargo mass is recorded in a separate field.

fields.label: Passengers carried
fields.help: The original 12-passenger regulation sets an upper limit of 12 passengers, subject to its stated activities and exclusions.

fields.label: Operating in the waters of § 1
fields.help: Norwegian territorial waters, including those at Svalbard, and rivers and lakes covered by the Norwegian 12-passenger regulation.

fields.label: Date built
fields.help: Use the statutory build date. The post-1998 wheelhouse-visibility clause turns on the date built.

fields.label: Build contract signed
fields.help: The transitional rule uses the contract date together with the date of delivery.

fields.label: Date delivered
fields.help: Supply the contractual delivery record for the transition test in § 9.

fields.label: Keel laid or equivalent stage
fields.help: The transition rule gives a separate date for ships built without a contract.

fields.label: Built under a contract
fields.help: Select the applicable construction route before evaluating transitional dates.

fields.label: Last qualifying vessel-instruction survey
fields.help: Use the full or periodic control by an approved undertaking under § 149. For the 2014 text see § 83, which refers to the full or periodic simplified control. The six-month early window may preserve an earlier anniversary.

fields.label: Has a wheelhouse
fields.help: Section 19(1) includes this condition for the post-1998 visibility requirements.

fields.label: Will tow
fields.help: Towing is one of the operations triggering a vessel instruction under § 2(1).

fields.label: Will handle anchors
fields.help: Apply the definition in § 5(a) when completing the § 2(1)(b) test.

fields.label: Maximum cargo carried
fields.help: Use maximum carried cargo mass. The threshold in § 2(1)(c) is strictly greater than 1,000 kg.

fields.label: Heeling arm from lifting
fields.help: Use the heeling arm from the lifting appliance. The original 2014 rule defines the arm as heeling moment divided by displacement.

fields.label: Transfers people to offshore renewable installations
fields.help: The activity described in § 2(1)(e) includes transfer between ship and an installation for offshore renewable electricity production.

fields.label: Approved recreational competency training
fields.help: Section 1(4) concerns approved educational establishments providing training for recreational-craft certificates of competence.

fields.label: Exclusively within the 2020 passenger rules
fields.help: Confirm both coverage under Regulation 2020-01-14-63 and exclusive operation as described there, assessed at the relevant date.

fields.label: Exclusively within the 2009 passenger rules
fields.help: Historical 2014 wording refers to Regulation 2009-11-24-1400 and exclusive operation as described there.

fields.label: Certified medical or school transport
fields.help: The passenger rule excludes medical or ambulance service or organized school transport where the vessel must hold a passenger certificate.

fields.label: Ship’s tender carrying passengers ashore
fields.help: The passenger rule excludes boats forming part of a ship’s equipment and carrying passengers between ship and shore.

fields.label: Trading certificate required
fields.help: Use the statutory requirement for a fartssertifikat. Section 1(2) limits chapters 6–14 to ships required to have a trading certificate or a vessel instruction.

fields.label: School or kindergarten boating-safety activity
fields.help: The 2020 passenger regulation treats sea-safety activities run by schools, school camps or kindergartens separately.

fields.label: Members’ club or association recreation
fields.help: This covers a vessel used by members of a club or association for leisure activities under the passenger regulation.

fields.label: Norwegian mainland territorial waters
fields.help: The small-vessel power table in § 2(1)(c) specifies mainland territorial waters. The jurisdiction in § 1 is broader.

fields.label: Maximum propulsion power
fields.help: Use the rated maximum in kW for the power table in § 2(1)(c). Use zero for an unpowered boat. The four overall-length bands have different limits.

fields.label: An exclusion in regulation 4(2) or 4(3) applies
fields.help: Check the full regulation for your date, including ship classes, fishing, pleasure use and circumstances of entry. The high-speed craft reference changed on 19 December 2022.

fields.label: High-speed craft subject to the referenced UK regulations
fields.help: Use the High Speed Craft Regulations cited at the research date: the 2004 Regulations before 19 December 2022 and the 2022 Regulations from that date.

fields.label: UK statutory ship class
fields.help: Use the class assigned under Schedule 2 of this instrument. These are statutory service classes.

fields.label: Keel laid or similar construction stage
fields.help: Use the date the keel was laid or the date the ship reached the similar stage defined by regulation 2. Completion and delivery dates refer to different milestones.

fields.label: International voyage under regulation 2
fields.help: Use the ports and Convention-country definition printed in regulation 2.

fields.label: U.S. Part 175 operating area
fields.help: Choose waters subject to U.S. jurisdiction or the high seas beyond territorial seas for a boat owned in the United States.

options.label: U.S.-owned boat on the high seas beyond territorial seas

fields.label: A § 175.1(a)–(e) exclusion applies
fields.help: The full list covers foreign boats temporarily using U.S. waters, specified military or public boats, state government boats, ships’ lifeboats and seaplanes on the water.

fields.label: Recreational vessel within § 175.11
fields.help: Use §§ 175.3 and 175.11 to check the definition of recreational vessel and the means of propulsion or control.

fields.label: Length for the § 175.15 flotation rule
fields.help: Enter the length in feet used to apply § 175.15(b).

fields.label: An exemption under § 175.17 applies
fields.help: For the additional throwable device, check canoes and kayaks of at least 16 feet, racing craft, sailboards and the qualifying foreign-competitor case.

fields.label: Operating in New Zealand waters
fields.help: Part 91 applies throughout New Zealand waters under rule 91.3.

fields.label: Original Part 91 bylaw and transition conditions apply
fields.help: For the 2003 signed rule, check whether the area had navigation bylaws, their consistency with Part 91 and the transition until 31 March 2004 in 91.3(2)–(3).

fields.label: Recreational craft under rule 91.2
fields.help: The definition includes a pleasure craft or a vessel powered solely by hand or solely by sail.

fields.label: New Zealand Part 91 length overall
fields.help: Rule 91.2 includes projecting structures such as buoyancy tubing and excludes specified fittings such as bowsprits and outboard drive units. Use this length in metres for the six-metre test in 91.4(1A).

fields.label: Craft underway under rule 91.2
fields.help: Underway excludes a vessel at anchor, made fast to the shore or aground.

fields.label: An exception to rule 91.4(1A) applies to this person
fields.help: Check swimming under (1B), the activities and equipment in (2), a qualifying support vessel in (4) and any written regional exemption under (5).

fields.label: Both vessels are in a harbour area defined by bylaw
fields.help: Check the regional navigation bylaw. Rule 91.16(2) defines harbour area for this duty.

fields.label: Other vessel's gross tonnage
fields.help: Use the gross tonnage of the vessel whose navigation could be impeded.

fields.help: The treaty gives dhows and junks as examples of traditional builds.

fields.label: Warship or naval auxiliary
fields.help: Article II(4) expressly excludes these ships.

fields.label: International voyage under Regulation 5.1.3
fields.help: For this regulation the voyage must be from a country to a port outside that country.

fields.label: Operating from or between ports in another country

fields.label: Shipowner requested MLC certification
fields.help: Under Regulation 5.1.3(2) the shipowner may request certification from the member whose flag the vessel flies.

Voyage under SOLAS I/2(d)
fields.help: The voyage must run between a country to which SOLAS applies and a port outside that country, in either direction.

fields.label: Does a listed SOLAS vessel exception describe the ship?
fields.help: Rule I/3(a) lists these categories. The separate cargo-ship tonnage test is evaluated independently. Other SOLAS chapters can expressly apply.

fields.label: Sailing solely within the I/3(b) Great Lakes–St Lawrence boundary
fields.help: Use the line from Cap des Rosiers to West Point on Anticosti Island and the 63rd meridian north of the island. Chapter V has its own provisions.

fields.label: Passengers counted under SOLAS I/2(e)
fields.help: Exclude the master, crew, persons working on the ship's business and children under one year of age. More than 12 makes a passenger ship for this definition.

fields.label: Ship's gross tonnage for this SOLAS threshold
fields.help: Use the tonnage applicable to SOLAS on the ship's official records for the date in question. Historical tonnage treatment can differ. This is a tonnage measure, distinct from deadweight.
